title: Reducing Data for AES-256 Key Recovery up to 10 Rounds
summary: The paper describes key-recovery attacks on AES-256 variants with up to 10 rounds, but whether they can use fewer chosen plaintexts or ciphertexts remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether the data complexity of the key-recovery attacks on $\mathrm{AES}\text{-}256$ variants with up to $10$ rounds can be reduced by lowering the number of required chosen plaintexts or chosen ciphertexts.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptanalysis of key-recovery attacks on AES-256 variants with up to 10 rounds.
parameters: Round count: at most 10 rounds in the targeted AES-256 variants
Number of chosen plaintexts or chosen ciphertexts: the data-complexity quantity to be reduced
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the attacks can be modified to require fewer chosen plaintexts or chosen ciphertexts.

citations.label: Key Recovery Attacks of Practical Complexity on AES-256 Variants with up to 10 Rounds

progress.summary: The source lists this question in its Conclusions and Open Problems section after presenting practical attacks that require large chosen-plaintext or chosen-ciphertext data sets.
citation_labels: Alex Biryukov et al., Key Recovery Attacks of Practical Complexity on AES-256 Variants with up to 10 Rounds
